summary: Jules Oppert worked in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums, Heidelberg, Bonn, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Kiel. He was a professor at Collège de France (1874–1905) and the University of Paris (~1874–1905).

Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University before holding a post at the University of Toronto (~1978–2001).

Julia F. Andrews specializes in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University. She served as director of the Institute for Chinese Studies at Ohio State University.
Julia Leslie worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies. She founded and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1993–2004).

Julian Strube specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Amsterdam. His posts include Heidelberg (2015–2019), Amsterdam (2016–2017), the University of Münster (2019–2021), and the University of Vienna (~2021).

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University around 1991.

Julie A. Gifford works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Paul J. Griffiths, and held a post at Miami University.

Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Royal Asiatic Society, University College London, and the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Strasbourg and its library (~1871/1872–1909).

Julius Grill worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn at the University of Tübingen, later serving as professor at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1871–1888) and at Tübingen (1888).

Julius Jolly was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and also studied under Martin Haug. From ~1877 to 1923, he served as a professor at the University of Würzburg.

Julius Lipner works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, the University of Birmingham, and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Birmingham (~1973–1975) and the University of Cambridge (~1975–2013).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1999–2005) and held a teaching post as a lecturer at Komazawa University (~2012–2016).

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and at Kyoto University. He held posts at JSPS, Aichi Prefectural University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1992–2020).

Jundo Nagashima works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Kojun Saito, Alexis Sanderson, and doctoral supervisor Paul Williams at the University of Bristol. He has served as a lecturer at Taisho University.

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She completed an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago before becoming a professor at the College of Charleston in ~1988.

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn, and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, later becoming a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe, Sheila Dillon, Richard M. Jaffe, and Wei-Cheng Lin.

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Ryukoku, Tokyo, and Oxford, training with Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1897–1927), Osaka, Toyo, and Musashino.
Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Toyo University until ~1894, he held posts at Toyo University, Sendan-Rin School, and Komazawa University.
